title: Algebraic equivalence of invertible modules by smooth connected families
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. For invertible modules $M,N$ on $X$ [def-sc-invertible-module], define algebraic equivalence as the equivalence relation on their isomorphism classes generated by pairs of fibres of an invertible module $P$ on $X\times_k T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], where $T$ is a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The two fibres are tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback] along $X\to X\times_kT$, $x\mapsto(x,t_i)$, for $t_0,t_1\in T(k)$. Equivalently on representatives, take the reflexive symmetric transitive closure of isomorphic pairs and pairs isomorphic to these fibres, and require both endpoints to be invertible. Smoothness supplies geometric reducedness, so these parameter schemes are precisely smooth connected varieties in the source convention.

source.place: Chapter I §8 (Picard families), Remark 10.19 (p.50), and conventions on varieties (p.v); the fibre-generated equivalence relation is specified explicitly in lem-sfb-abelian-multiplication-algebraic-equivalence.
